canonical_topic: Variable Pricing Components in Physical Crude Contracts (Index + Differentials, CMA)
definition: Variable-priced physical crude oil contracts are built from a futures-linked index price adjusted by grade, location, and other differentials, with the index itself often defined using a calendar month average.
core_idea: A variable-priced physical crude deal typically references an index price (commonly the next-to-deliver, or 'prompt', futures contract) plus differentials for crude grade, delivery location, and other negotiated factors; because many crude contracts don't expire at month end, index pricing is often defined instead as a Calendar Month Average (CMA) rather than tied to one specific futures contract.
key_points: Index Price: commonly the next-to-deliver ('prompt') crude oil futures contract
Grade Differential (also called basis): a premium or discount to the index depending on the crude grade/quality
Location Differential (also called basis): a premium or discount reflecting the cost to transport oil to the delivery location, e.g. pipeline or trucking fees
Other Differential: a premium or discount arising from other negotiated factors
Because many crude oil futures contracts don't expire at month end, a common way to define the index price is a Calendar Month Average (CMA) rather than a single specific futures settlement
relationships: WTI and Brent as Global Crude Oil Benchmarks
trading_implications: Traders decompose physical crude pricing into an index plus differentials, which lets them hedge the index leg via futures while separately negotiating grade/location/other basis

formulas.name: Variable physical crude price (conceptual)
formulas.formula: Physical Price = Index Price + Grade Differential + Location Differential + Other Differential

variables.Index Price: typically the prompt (next-to-deliver) futures price, sometimes a Calendar Month Average (CMA)
variables.Grade Differential: premium/discount for crude quality/grade, also called basis
variables.Location Differential: premium/discount for transport cost to delivery point, also called basis
